records.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR name 911 GT1-98 maps to Porsche's all-new 1998 GT1 race car, not the 1996 911 GT1, 1997 911 GT1 Evo, or the separate 1998 911 GT1-98 Straßenversion. Porsche's own Museum and Newsroom material identify the 1998 works/customer race specification and its six-speed sequential gearbox.
records.confidence_basis: Porsche Museum's exact 911 GT1 '98 data sheet identifies the 1998 FIA GT customer car as technically identical to the Le Mans-winning factory car and states the six-speed sequential gearbox. Porsche Newsroom independently identifies the 1998 overhauled race car and its Zakspeed FIA GT use. The PMR telemetry name and GT1 class match the existing curated identity.

records.specification_basis: Porsche Museum explicitly states a sequential six-speed gearbox; the independent specification page also lists six speeds. The technical feature places the gear selector to the driver's right and describes its pull-back/push-forward operation; the exact GT1/98-004 cockpit photograph visibly shows the lever beside the driver. Porsche identifies the six-speed gearbox as sequential, and the article describes sequential fore/aft selector movement: pull back for upshifts and push forward for downshifts. Ortelli's direct recollection says the 1998 car could not be flat-shifted. The conservative control interpretation is that a full-throttle upshift was not the authentic procedure and the driver had to lift or otherwise unload the drivetrain. Manual blipping is a downshift action in this control model; no upshift blip claim is being made. Automatic blipping is a downshift action in this control model; no upshift blip claim is being made. Throttle-lift is recorded as an upshift action in this control model; no separate downshift-lift claim is asserted. Automatic cut is recorded as an upshift action in this control model; no downshift-cut claim is asserted. The full-resolution photograph of identified chassis GT1/98-004 shows a conventional racing rim with a flattened lower section and open upper section, rather than a continuous round rim or a fixed-grip GT-formula face. The exact-chassis cockpit photograph visibly shows the upper section of the conventional rim removed. The article states that the digital gear indicator was on the panel, and the exact-chassis photo shows the display mounted behind the rim rather than integrated into the wheel. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights.

The downshift blip is not established, so that much is the cautious default rather than this car's known technique.
